title: A Swing at 19:57
setup: February 21, 2000, in Vancouver. With three seconds left in the third period, Bruins enforcer Marty McSorley strikes Canucks forward Donald Brashear on the head with his stick. McSorley is given a match penalty under Rule 52, deliberate injury of an opponent. League discipline chief Colin Campbell holds a hearing on February 23.
question: How is McSorley punished?
options: At least the rest of the season, playoffs included
ruling: Campbell suspended McSorley for at least the rest of the 1999-2000 season, including the playoffs, the longest suspension in league history for an on-ice incident. McSorley chose not to attend the hearing, and Campbell said the videotape made the facts clear. He missed the Bruins' remaining 23 regular-season games and all playoff games, forfeited $72,000 and had to meet with commissioner Gary Bettman before the next season.
rulebookNote: The source describes the suspension as lasting at least the rest of the season, with a meeting with the commissioner required before he could return.
